newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: KEPPEL SINKS TO NEW FOUR YEAR LOW.
newsitem.headline: KEPPEL SINKS TO NEW FOUR YEAR LOW.

text.p: Keppel Corp Ltd shares sank to a new four year low of Singapore $5.95 on Thursday in active dealings.
At 0347 GMT, the stock was down 20 cents at S$6.00. Volume was an active 2.98 million.
The last time the ship-repair conglomerate was trading at these levels was in July 31, 1993 when it closed at S$6.00.
Dealers and analysts said the fall was probably due to market talk of poor interim earnings.

"The market is looking for a drop of six to seven percent in interim profit for the group. But this figure has been out for about a month. Maybe some fund managers are just waking up to this," said an analyst with a European stockbroking firm.
Keppel Corp reported interim net profits of S$100 million in 1996.
Analysts also said there was concern over why Keppel, which traditionally releases its results in early August, has not been able to do so this year.
"There is more speculation that results are bad because of this delay," said one analyst.
Keppel officials have said the group would not release its results this week but have not indicated when it might be.
